findings.title: A diagram can hide its own parse error as "unreachable", and a sandbox failure is called a broken diagram
quotes: when it exits non-zero with `Parse error` in its output
findings.fix: test `Parse error` first (non-zero exit only), and make everything else "unreachable", as CT-3 says. Don't match the markers against output that can contain diagram text.

sources.situation: `render` checks `any(m in both for m in COULD_NOT_RUN)` before it looks for `Parse error`. mermaid-cli prints the offending source text in a parse error. A diagram with a syntax error and a label or node containing `ENOTFOUND`, `npm ERR` or `ETIMEDOUT` therefore returns "unreachable". `check` treats that as no error, so a broken diagram passes. The opposite also happens. Any non-zero exit without a marker and without `Parse error` is returned as `broken: <first line>`. Examples are a puppeteer "No usable sandbox" error when running as root or in CI, an OOM kill, or an unknown renderer crash. CT-3 says these are "unreachable". The check then fails with `broken diagram: <title>` for a valid diagram, and the writer is told to fix a diagram that is fine.

`render("flowchar TD", ...)` against a mermaid-cli that exits 1 with `UnknownDiagramError: No diagram type detected` (no `Parse error` text). CT-3 says `unreachable`. The code (`if r.returncode == 0 or any(m in both for m in COULD_NOT_RUN):`, then `return "broken: " + next((l for l in lines if "Parse error" in l), lines[0] if lines else "exit %d" % r.returncode)`) returns `broken`, and the diff's own test asserts `explain.render("flowchar TD", Path(d) / "o.svg").startswith("broken: UnknownDiagramError"), "typo"`. The approved CT-3 wording was not changed and no change request appears in the pack; the test was written to match the code.

a block with the typo `flowchar TD` makes npx exit 1 with `UnknownDiagramError`. The code returns `broken: UnknownDiagramError...` and the check names that block. Under CT-3 it returns `unreachable`, so `nio check explainer` prints `render skipped: the renderer could not be fetched` and stops rendering (the `break` in the check and in finish). Every later block is then never checked and the check can pass with a broken diagram in it. The test in tests/test_explain.py (test_ac9_broken_block) asserts the code's behaviour, so the approved text and the tests disagree.

findings.reason: explain.py:84 tests the COULD_NOT_RUN markers against the whole output before `Parse error`, so diagram text can mask a parse error; and a non-zero exit with no marker returns `broken:` where CT-3 says "any other failure" is `unreachable`. test_ac9 asserts `broken: UnknownDiagramError`, which contradicts CT-3.

sources.situation: `nodes` only counts IDs that are `[A-Za-z_]\w*`, sit next to the arrows in `ARROW`, or stand alone on a line. Each of these gives a diagram of 21 or more nodes that counts 20 or fewer.

the passing test_ac5_node_cap proves only the node count. It doesn't prove that `nio check explainer` fails naming a 21-node diagram. The test that does is test_ac5_node_cap_check at tests/test_explain.py:146, and it has no result in the evidence file.

`nodes()` does `line.split(":")[0]` before it splits on arrows. A Mermaid class shorthand such as `A:::hot --> B:::hot --> C:::hot --> ...` therefore yields only `A`. A 40-node chain written that way counts as 1 node, `check explainer` exits 0, and the oversized diagram ships. Diagram types with no arrow endpoints (class diagrams `Animal <|-- Duck`, ER `A ||--o{ B`, mindmap, gantt) are also under-counted, because only `-->`-style arrows and `participant`/`state` lines are recognised. Nothing fails or warns, so the rule meant to keep diagrams readable silently stops applying.

findings.reason: `nodes` only counts IDs matching `[A-Za-z_]\w*` next to ARROW matches. A diagram with numeric IDs (`1 --> 2`) never passes the fullmatch, so it counts 0. The cap in FR-7 is bypassed with no note.

findings.title: A mermaid block can fall outside `sections` and `check`, and nothing says so
quotes: Given a diagram block with a syntax error, when the check runs, then it fails naming that block as a broken diagram.
findings.fix: compare the first word of the fence case-insensitively. Look at every fenced block in a section. Report an unclosed fence as an error.

sources.situation: `sections` records only the first fenced block of a section (CT-1, "the section's first fenced block"). `check` renders only when `s["fence"] == "mermaid"`, an exact, case-sensitive match. These cases all produce no error and no note.

a section holds a small first Mermaid block and then a second block with a syntax error or 60 nodes. `sections()` keeps only the first (`if cur["block"] is None:`). `check` therefore never counts nodes in the second block and never renders it, so no `broken diagram` appears. A first block fenced `Mermaid` or `mmd` instead of `mermaid` is also skipped silently (`s["fence"] == "mermaid"` is an exact match). The check passes and finish later renders or links only the first block, so the second never reaches the reader as a checked diagram.

findings.reason: `sections` keeps only the first block, and `check` (line 130) and `finish` (line 241) compare the fence to `mermaid` exactly. An unclosed fence leaves `block` None, and `check` raises nothing outside the core sections.

An explainer with N diagrams makes the check run about 120 x N seconds, and a hook or CI step looks hung. The ponytail comment says T-4 adds the skip, but this diff ships the loop without the stop and without the note.
